Let’s dive into Chapter 5—Designing Mobility and Embracing Remote Work as a Default.
Now that you’ve got income streams rolling in, and you’ve freed up your time from all those unnecessary tasks, there’s one last piece to this part of the journey: creating a life that isn’t tied to any one place.
Thanks to digital tools and the way we’re all connected around the globe, you can work, learn, and just live—almost anywhere you want.
But here’s the thing—mobility isn’t just about packing your bags and traveling the world. It’s really about having the freedom to choose where and how you live.
Maybe you dream of being a digital nomad, hopping between cities or countries throughout the year. Or maybe you’d rather settle somewhere with a lower cost of living, or just have the flexibility to spend more time with your family, or out in nature.
Making the jump to remote work and a more mobile lifestyle does mean thinking through some practical stuff.
First up— negotiating remote arrangements. If you’re in a more traditional job, you might be surprised how open companies can be to remote work, especially if you can show them you’re even more productive this way. You could start with a trial run, or just a few days a week, and build trust from there.
Next, there’s setting up your mobile office. Really, with a laptop, strong internet, and a handful of the right tools, you can do most knowledge work from anywhere. Cloud storage, communication apps, and project management platforms make it easy to collaborate, no matter where you are.
Of course, there are some details to keep an eye on—like visas, taxes, health insurance, and time zones. Planning ahead and using services built for remote workers can make these transitions way smoother.
So, what are some smart strategies for making mobility work?
Well, start by testing the waters. Try short trips or a remote work experiment before you make any big moves.
Then, focus on building routines—set up daily habits and workspaces that help you stay focused and feel good, no matter where you are.
And don’t forget to stay connected. Use tech to keep in touch with your coworkers, clients, and loved ones, even if you’re halfway around the world.
The real magic in mobility is designing your life around what matters most to you. Instead of cramming life into the small spaces left by work, you get to flip the script.
It’s about taking back control—choosing where you want to live, when you want to work, and what you’ll do with each day.
This chapter is really about unlocking that last layer of freedom: geographic independence. Imagine seeing the world as a menu of possibilities and building a life that feels both grounded and wide open at the same time.
So far, you’ve challenged old ideas, cut out the stuff you don’t need, and put systems in place to support real freedom.
Up next? We’re going to dive even deeper—looking at advanced strategies for keeping your momentum, facing challenges, and making the most out of your new, redesigned workweek and life.
